newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices rebound on futures rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices rebound on futures rally.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices rebounded Wednesday on the heels of a rallying futures market, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices gained more than five cents to about $2.15 per mmBtu, with Henry Hub quoted at $2.17-2.20 and Transco (Station 65) pegged around $2.17-2.18.
NYMEX's July Henry Hub gas futures rose to a high of $2.17, up 6.7 cents.
The rising futures also pushed south Texas prices several cents higher to about $2.10, traders said.
Keeping a lid on prices, however, were forecasts calling for more cool temperatures throughout most of the East, upper Midwest and Northwest this week, according to Weather Services Corp (WSC).
Despite cooler forecasts in the Southwest, temperature highs in Phoenix are expected to remain above 100 degrees F through Friday, WSC reported.
The stronger Gulf values also filtered into the west Texas market as Permian prices rose cents to about $2.00-2.01.
Southern California prices, however, held at $2.12-2.13 as temperature highs stretched only into the mid-70s in Los Angeles, according to WSC.
In the Midwest, prices climbed nearly five cents to about $2.02-2.04, with Chicago city-gate prices talked around $2.23-2.25.
New York city gate prices followed suit by regaining five to 10 cents to $2.40-2.45.
